## Changed processing and memory argument

The fixed Rust 1.100.0 proof convention and unmodified history arithmetic from issue #4 remain applicable. Changed paths are the shared pure check extraction, per-transaction admission mask, per-current-transaction application mask and invalid-pair finalization. Masks have at most128 registered keys each, with u32 key/u8 value. Validation drains its map between transactions; application builds/drains only the current transaction. No mask per whole batch is retained. Both maps, including retained empty roots, are charged simultaneously by `2 * tree_bytes::<u32,u8>(128)` = **9516 bytes**, replacing the old single u32/unit tree charge of4472. This adds5044 to the existing private metadata reservation, not to its 8-MiB allowance.

Rust's existing 11-key/12-edge, five-key minimum-occupancy derivation still applies: node bound26, each conservatively128 +11*(4+1)=183 bytes, one map4758. Independent heap measurement of two simultaneously filled/drained new typed maps observed **3600 bytes** peak against9516 reserved. This measurement checks the actual changed type, including retained roots; it supplements the general node argument rather than proving arbitrary allocator/RSS behavior.

Work remains sliced under the existing outer64 + per-dispatch64 accounting. Validation map insertion/cleanup remains <=240 tree primitives plus fixed mask control under256. Ordinary application adds one <=240 map operation to the existing <=128 raw lookup (or unchanged bounded market-reset work); it remains under its1024 reservation. Finalization reserves512: one <=240 map pop plus <=128 raw search and fixed scalar/mask clearing. Rejection cleanup pops one entry at a time. Shared pure descriptor checks retain the same bounded three128-byte identity scans,128 catalog visits and association loops, with actual instrumentation; no copied whitelist or per-binding requirement allocation is introduced. Existing unaffected heavy branches remain at their prior reservations. The independent whole-slice probe in the new128-binding/256-member invalid-pair case observed **2907 primitives maximum**, below4096; all existing branch/extrema/continuation/resource probes passed in the final engine test run. This is algorithmic work, not a latency claim.

Source-owned state: max64 allocated requirement slots (<=34 live),128 binding slots,4 market slots (<=2 live),6 streams and3 connections; no raw book, frame queue or historical series. On this arm64 compiler, measured inline sizes are owner272, Bound304, BindingView320, SourceRequirement88, StampEntry32 and Market96 bytes. Each retained binding owns <=320 descriptor-text bytes plus <=256 provenance bytes; requirements own <=100 bytes each; markets own <=384 bytes each; current ID<=128 and retained selected series<=128. Conservative retained owner bound:272 +64*88 +34*100 +128*(304+576) +4*96 +2*384 +128 +128 = **123352 bytes**, below128KiB. Insertion, clone-normalized strings and caps prevent hidden retained input capacities; source-only handoffs reuse the existing allocation and release retired payloads.

One returned typed view owns <=128*(320+676) binding bytes plus bounded current/next/source/stream headers, below160KiB before the stricter construction guard. The guard additionally charges2048 fixed/header bytes,512 per market and1024 per binding for keys/scalars/variants plus TWO bytes per text byte (maximum escaping when controls are excluded), and refuses above256KiB. It is a conservative representation allowance, not a newly published native JSON/IPC schema. A later wire projection must enforce its own approved decimal-string counters/envelope cap.

One owned normalized input plus one effect fits a conservative128KiB each: <=128 update/binding records with bounded text, <=256 EvidenceChange slots (or two128-member revocation vectors), <=128 coverage facts/stamp entries, at most4 transaction allocation slots and at most2 current/next registrations. Scratch uses bounded scans, at most128 borrowed matching references per requirement, and no elapsed-time loop. Owner + one input + one effect + one view + constructor overlap stays below1MiB from these type/collection bounds, separately from unchanged evaluator history/metadata/ingress admission. Caller-retained older clones and allocator arenas/RSS are outside that contract. No performance/capacity qualification is inferred.

### Supported Spec findings and lead verification

**R1 — P1: metadata-only invalidation leaves a prepared ask-only market and its old stamps usable.** sources.rs:1021 dispatches invalidation to stream-assigned Bound records. Ask-only requirements have no Metadata Bound record; Market.verified and market_revision are not revoked. The approved plan requires metadata/schedule uncertainty to revoke preparation and relevant metadata/preparation revisions to fence results. The lead reproduced a prepared market → invalidate(Stream::Metadata, MetadataChanged) → old ask stamp still current, Preparation::Ready, zero revocation transactions, and an emitted next-opening boundary. Correct the shared metadata invalidation path to revoke market preparation/stamps even without a reference binding, require re-verification before promotion, and add that timeline.

**R2 — P1: first source readiness at opening can produce a candidate in that same window.** sources.rs:950–955 tests readiness at opening but retains no initial source-readiness time. The ask-only evaluator initializes ready_at=Some(0) for zero-history requirements (strategy.rs:2665 onward); its guard cannot establish source availability before opening. Controlled timeline: connect at0, first initialization/verification at open1, Boundary1 and a valid controlled objective. The lead observed source_opening_transaction_count=1 and Some(Candidate{market_id:m,option_id:buy,side:Yes,remaining_quantity:1}). No order was submitted. This violates the plan's “Initial readiness exactly at opening still waits for a later full market.” Track/gate initial source readiness strictly before the first eligible opening, preserving active-run recovery, and add a source/evaluator boundary regression. The earlier review's generic readiness-guard reasoning missed the zero-history constructor case; this concrete reproduction supersedes that inference without rewriting the historical report.

**R3 — P2: constructor allocates an oversized identity before rejecting it.** sources.rs:347 clones the borrowed first series_id before market-count/identity-length checks. The lead supplied a synthetic2MiB series ID and independently measured a2097152-byte allocation during SourceState::new before rejection. This violates the explicit reject-before-copy admission rule. ### Finding 1 — Must fix: current window opened before Go is rejected

**What this is:** The source owner retains the current market plus its immediate successor. Clock values are elapsed milliseconds since Go (approved step2 plan:76), while the existing MarketDescriptor uses signed open/close times; a current window may have opened before zero. The design requires current/next records and permits late current-market display without entering that missed window (market-data-design:333–344).

**Problem:** sources.rs:404 adds open_ms<0 rejection beyond the existing shared descriptor validator. A valid current descriptor open=-60000/close=840000 plus successor open=840000/close=1740000 is accepted by Evaluator::new but rejected by SourceState::new as identity_mismatch. This blocks the bounded current+next setup even though it neither imports pre-Go observations nor requests entry into the current window. Both source construction and later RegisterMarket call the same rejecting validate_market path. The source also casts descriptor times to u64 in admission, Boundary, retirement and usability, so removing that guard alone would mishandle these signed times.

**Fix:** Admit valid current-window metadata whose opening precedes Go and use the evaluator's existing signed-time comparison pattern for all source schedule comparisons (current locations568–569,983,987,1027,1218). Preserve first-full-window entry and post-Go-only history. Add a public current+next registration parity test with a negative current opening, late/display-only handling, next-boundary eligibility and expired-window retirement. No new clock framework, configuration or dependency is needed.

**If skipped:** A normal registration during an already-open market fails initialization or loses the required current-market display/preparation path. The current module is not yet wired to provider or financial execution, so this is a demonstrated controlled-boundary bug, not evidence of a live order problem.

Lead reproduced the mismatch in a disposable standalone copy of the exact frozen candidate with existing public helpers: market(m,-60000),market(n,840000), four correct YES/NO bindings, matching series and validated ask rules. Correction stays on that path. The existing in-flight socket guard now records a
completed send/receive failure once with the existing Retry owner and still
closes/revokes the socket. Dropping an unfinished public operation resets usable
continuity with Stopped, without inventing a failed network attempt. Transient
I/O, EOF/abrupt loss and received Close are distinguished from malformed protocol;
the same classifier covers reads, control writes and protocol flushes. No new
retry loop is introduced. Deadline remains the existing finite Deadline result:
it resets socket usability but is not newly counted as Transport, so local permit
expiry/caller cancellation cannot consume a transient-attempt count. HTTP/handshake
timeout policy is otherwise unchanged by this established-socket correction.

**Verdict: revise finding 1 before implementation.**

1. **Must fix — define changed-descriptor recovery.** Plan lines 103–105 require
   changed-schedule revalidation/handoff; line 168 expects no engine production
   edits. For a retained successor N whose verified opening changes from 12:15,
   SourceState::Metadata only toggles verified and continues using the retained
   descriptor (sources.rs 938–975). RegisterMarket rejects an existing market ID
   (400–408) and a third retained market (885–889). Re-verification of unchanged
   descriptors in sources tests does not establish replacement. The approved
   design's changed-schedule recovery therefore has no specified realizable path.
   Define the owner-controlled transition before implementation: narrow source
   descriptor replacement/retirement with public tests and contract/inventory
   updates if recovery must preserve the context, or an explicit stopped/new-context
   policy reconciled with promised behavior. Cover same ticker/changed schedule,
   old completion, fresh metadata and recovered data. Do not add a second mutable
   native schedule. Skipping this leaves an unplanned engine change, unrecoverable
   market or risk of re-verifying stale times. This is a static interface finding,
   not a reproduced runtime defect in the existing app.

### Implemented behavior and corrections

- Kalshi reconstructs both retained YES/NO books, derives complementary asks,
  preserves quantity/clock/sequence, checks sequence before irrelevant-ticker
  filtering and recovers both books independently on the same socket. Empty
  liquidity expires the absent binding; later reconstruction can initialize it.
  Trade identity ledgers fail capacity rather than evict. BRTI raw values remain
  separate from average/count/window details. Known command rejection disables
  its scope; unknown error codes do not become invented entitlement findings.
- Coinbase and Kraken validate fixed products, snapshots/initialization, monotone
  identity, same-price new observations and replay/conflict behavior. Kraken
  validates the whole bounded batch before publication and chooses the newest
  snapshot identity even when its array is descending. Prices retain exact
  six-place USD or six-place cents meaning; incompatible precision is refused.
- Six startup/four successor metadata GETs, two-page/400-candidate bounds,
  canonical-series/detail validation, opaque cursor encoding, 60/30/10 checks and
  paced post-opening fallback use existing budgets. Expired metadata cannot
  readmit a retired slot. Prepared rollover retires before adding, preserves
  underlying identities and performs no boundary-search GET. Same-ticker schedule
  replacement revokes before revalidation; entered source contexts stop. A
  controlled evaluator with an immutable old catalog must stop and recover with
  an explicit fresh pair/epoch, retaining old history only as stopped evidence.
- Reader/writer halves are concurrently polled inside each of the three owned
  provider futures. Progress/control wakes retain the same pending receive. A
  late old-token frame cannot restore evidence; one coalesced counted snapshot
  retry can obtain the replacement under the next receive identity. ACK and
  first/replacement-data deadlines remain separate. Progress starts with the
  captured tokens, avoiding redundant initial recovery controls.
- Metadata/connection/gap changes clear reconstruction baselines. Per-market book
  and trade details retire with their slot. Native permission epochs, session and
  worker fences invalidate retained views before more ordinary work. Exhausted
  epochs never wrap. A nonqueued scheduling-loss fact blocks market views until
  the worker applies core invalidation; a weaker fact cannot erase terminal loss.
  Only the worker owns the reanchored schedule epoch. Normal slow HTTP work alone
  is not treated as sleep. A delayed handshake rechecks identities and retained
  market membership before sending its initial subscriptions.
- Control receiver ownership returns through Drop even after task return, panic,
  cancellation or an unpolled future. Explicit recovery joins the old owner first.
  Shared retry state resets its usable interval on close/drop without adding a
  transient failure. Ping wakeups coalesce while automatic pongs remain independent
  of subscription permits. The keepalive counter counts explicit flush attempts,
  not every automatic wire pong. Existing total-deadline shutdown, retained
  unfinished handles and guarded engine-save behavior remain covered.

The original RegisterMarket-only schedule replacement failed its new regression;
`ReplaceMarket` corrects that demonstrated case. An early controlled three-provider
case with HTTP404 also exposed stale-generation handling that incorrectly ended
unrelated Kalshi work; the corrected test now retains BRTI and all seven initial
controls. Other lifecycle/parser corrections above came from static tracing and
focused tests added during implementation. Do not describe those as individually

ping-burst and shared retry interval cases pass on the final source; they were not
rerun against a reverted faulty tree. Intermediate compile/fixture/lint failures
were corrected; only the final results below are passing evidence.

### Retained resources and work argument

The fixed topology remains three provider tasks, one existing worker, one ordinary
raw slot, one metadata-command slot and seven finite mandatory controls per
provider. Recovery retains three replaceable stream records, not an event log;
scheduling invalidity retains one nonqueued fact. Socket reservations are 4 MiB
each (12 MiB total). Bounded raw ownership can include three receiving tasks,
one queued payload and one worker payload (5 MiB at the per-message maximum).
Worker decoding reserves 4 MiB before typed parsing. Each parsed metadata handoff
retains its 4-MiB permit through the command/reply payload until consumed/dropped;
HTTP bodies are at most 1 MiB and the bounded discovery collector reserves256 KiB.
Caller cancellation releases or transfers each owned reservation with its value.

Each retained book reservation is `2 * 8192 * 128 + 65536` = **2,162,688 bytes**.
Two books reserve4,325,376; a replacement coexisting with both reserves6,488,064,
below the separate8,388,608 two-book/overlap ceiling. The unchanged pinned Rust
1.100 BTree convention has11 keys/12 edges and minimum5-key occupancy; node count
is bounded from that occupancy. An i128-pair node plus edges is under512 bytes,
so128 bytes per level plus fixed headroom conservatively bounds these trees.
Each opaque trade identity reserves its text length plus2048 bytes for owned key/
record/node growth. IDs persist across reconnect until contract retirement, and
capacity fails explicitly; there is no uncharged ever-growing archive or eviction.

A shared64-KiB base permit follows the native context through worker, source handle
and provider futures. Every retained derived view reserves256 KiB before cloning;
this includes its bounded requirements, at most four per-market detail records,
three underlying detail records and fences in addition to the bounded core view.
The existing core view bound is below160 KiB; the additional bounded native
requirements/details/permissions remain inside256 KiB. Constructor overlap has
its own64-KiB reservation and initial temporary view256 KiB before retained copies.
All these adapter payload reservations use the same32-MiB owner, including bodies,
books, scratch and retained consumers. Independent maxima need not fit
simultaneously: admission refuses before growth when their combined reservation
would exceed32 MiB. This is a fail-closed allocation argument, not a claim that
all maximal workloads are supported or that SDK/TLS/kernel/allocator RSS is capped.
Step-6 measurement and capacity qualification remain pending.

SourceState's existing owner/input/effect/view/constructor proof stays below1 MiB,
separate from unchanged evaluator8-MiB/4096 work admission. ReplaceMarket checks
three bounded128-byte identities, the exact expected descriptor, two market slots,
nonoverlap/duration and revision headroom before commit. Old/replacement descriptor
text overlap is bounded to768 bytes plus fixed records, with no proportional
allocation for rejected input. It reuses bounded existing invalidation scans
(max128 bindings) and two-market selection; it introduces no elapsed-time loop or
history allocation. Native decoder work is bounded by the admitted1-MiB message,
depth48,16-KiB text and8192 entries per side. These are bounded work/input claims,
not measured wall-clock latency guarantees.

### Implemented route and maintained bounds

The [code map](../agents/code-map.md#step-5-source-setup-and-verification-route)
and [native contract](../../src-tauri/src/README.md#step-5-source-commands-and-isolated-receiver)
lead to the real owners and checks. Fixed engine display registration reuses the
existing validation owner without a fabricated strategy or evaluator. Native
`sources` and `provider_credential` decode exact finite requests, use fixed Demo
configuration, sanitize failures, and expose only local-main permissions. Local
snapshot/details/requirements reads do not connect or make provider requests.
No source activity starts merely by opening, refreshing, inspecting, saving a key
or starting the existing controlled session.

The same Coordinator, credential owner, SourceWorker/SourceState and transport
own the mutable facts. Four logical sources share three connections; Kalshi/BRTI
share the credential/socket while disconnect fences only the requested logical
source. Exclusive mutation work moves owned handles into blocking work and
restores them on failure. Pending Connect cannot undo a later Disconnect; checked
revocation revisions survive off/on watch coalescence. Credential replacement
stops/joins shared work before mutation. Quit revokes before waiting, retains
unfinished handles and refuses a false successful save/exit.

The display catalog has eight requirement records, three initial underlying
bindings and at most nineteen bindings with two retained markets. Existing
32-MiB adapter payload admission, two-book/8192-level-side bounds, one raw queue
slot/two-second age ceiling, three task slots and the engine's 8-MiB/4096-work
boundaries remain unchanged. No financial arithmetic, strategy semantics,
SQLite revision, Cargo dependency or pinned toolchain change. Snapshot/details
encode to at most256KiB; a512-KiB shared reservation remains owned through response
serialization. Source fixture envelopes are at most256KiB with128-KiB lexical
payload, with640KiB reserved for frame/decoded overlap plus the separately charged
intake copy. These are application ownership arguments, not RSS or capacity
qualification. No raised limit or granted freshness/history capability supplies
missing provider proof.

The sole validated bootstrap/descriptor reader selects dummy or Sources mode.
Sources mode is immutable and its ordinary credential/production transport paths
are refused, including after EOF/protocol failure. Exact session, canonical
string sequence and bounded envelopes feed the real decoder/worker. Ack1 follows
accepted or explicitly invalid published native state; it does not mean healthy
data or GUI paint. Cancellation, failed/late acknowledgment and receiver failure
revoke fixture evidence and retain owned shutdown handles.

The interface serializes local reads at the approved one-second active-screen

Findings (not corrected in this review):

1. **Must fix — failure reasons disappear before presentation.** In
   `providers/source.rs:wire_snapshot`, revoked stream permission replaces the
   recorded binding reason with `disconnected`. Coinbase malformed JSON calls
   `Fence::fail`, revokes gates and records InvalidValue; the wire response thus
   hides that cause. The packaged runner's subsequent wait for “Invalid source
   data” cannot succeed through this row. Separately, `view.mjs:sourcePresentation`

Original source inspection establishes:

- `providers/mod.rs:intake/admit` has one raw slot, nonblocking admission and fence
  revocation on overflow. `Intake` retains charged bytes, receipt time and captured
  source tokens. `transport.rs` has test-only loopback isolation and attempted
  request/control/data counters, not a completed-normalized-transaction ledger.
- `source.rs:Coordinator::start_sources` owns one thread, calls membership/loss/
  stop checks and `advance`, processes one item, publishes `SourceView` with a watch
  channel, then sleeps five milliseconds. Its current effects use `|_| Ok(())`;
  it has no financial evaluator. A fixture publication acknowledgment alone is
  therefore not evaluation completion and even an explicitly invalid frame can
  receive that acknowledgment.
- `SourceWorker::process/apply_source_event` calls the real Kalshi/Coinbase/Kraken
  decoders, exact lexical conversion and `SourceState::apply`. One frame can emit
  multiple effects/transactions. `SourceState` owns admission, validity and
  generations; it does not own history calculations. `Evaluator::begin` checks
  ingress plus private metadata; `process_slice` owns incremental completion and
  cleanup. `allocated_bytes()` is existing engine accounting, not process RSS.
- `providers/tests.rs:real_book_decoder_drives_learning_strategy_without_changing_its_rules`
  already drains effects through the public evaluator and asserts exact decisions.
  `all_source_strategy`, `source_markets`, `feed_source`, `book_frame`, owned-worker
  publication/stop tests and controlled transport helpers provide reusable setup.
  The all-source helper declares inputs but leaves learning decisions dependent
  on asks: extend test JSON explicitly so spot/history graphs actually evaluate
  the offered input. Do not mistake declared-but-unused inputs for graph load.
- Engine tests `phase1_hour_average_allocates_and_processes_admitted_workload`,
  `phase1_composed_history_runs_on_complete_normalized_clock`, and
  `phase1_registered_contract_hour_survives_its_exact_market_entry` provide graph,
  prehistory and ignored release-test conventions. Existing engine heap/work probes
  are private cfg(test) unit probes; they are not automatically active in the
  engine library linked into a native test executable.

provider calls and extra loopback/kernel buffering concealing the one-slot limit.
The worker remains the sole state writer. Instrumentation never treats a synthetic
producer as proof of real upstream delivery.

### Proposed fixtures, schedule and bounded experiment

Use release mode, serial tests, a fixed seed and declared deterministic tie order
(Kalshi, Coinbase, Kraken at coincident deadlines). Keep within-provider order and
legitimate multi-trade Kraken batches. Distinguish normalized price transactions
from frames, per-binding members, initialization, timer/control effects and
counter-only duplicates. The generator produces expected identities/counts
independently of observed completion; hash the actual templates/manifest first.

| Measured profile | Duration | Offered price transactions per second |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low | 900 seconds | 100: Kalshi books 9, Kalshi trades 10, BRTI 1, Coinbase 40, Kraken 40 |
| Medium | 900 seconds | 1,000: books 9, Kalshi trades 10, BRTI 1, Coinbase 490, Kraken 490 |
| Burst | 1 second | 10,000: books 9, Kalshi trades 10, BRTI 1, Coinbase 4,990, Kraken 4,990 |

These are synthetic stress mixes, not observed provider rates. BRTI is one genuine
index tick per second in every profile, with distinct identity/time; no extra
index ticks, averages or reference values are invented. Snapshot replacements
consume scheduled book slots instead of increasing the stated rate. Kraken uses
ordered groups of four trades plus the final remainder; each member counts as a
transaction, never just one frame. All other price frames contain one transaction.

Declare exact byte sizes before running: ordinary single-trade/index frames padded
with legal trailing JSON whitespace to 512 bytes; ordinary book frames 1,024 bytes;
four-trade Kraken frames 1,024 bytes (remainder frames also 1,024). Refuse fixture
generation if actual typed content exceeds its declared size; no truncation.
Record wire bytes and actual normalized ingress bytes separately. Include one
control/heartbeat per provider per second as separately counted additional frames,
never observations. Duplicate one scheduled spot identity every tenth second as
an additional marked duplicate frame, counted separately from the unique-price
rate. Initialization/ack frames are separately enumerated startup work.

Seed both retained books; at measured seconds 60, 300, 600 and 840 replace alternating
books with 4,096 levels per side in a 512-KiB padded valid snapshot. Include a
single such replacement in the burst's book slots. Validate exact decimals,
quantities, depth, level and simultaneous old/new allocation charges first; if this
snapshot cannot fit existing caps, record unsupported capacity and do not trim it
or substitute a smaller snapshot during the attempt. Maximum 8,192-level and
maximum/malformed-frame campaigns remain later qualification work. Exact generated
sizes/capacity expectations must be asserted by the short fixture self-check.

Three graph cases, each with a fresh owned pair and the same ladder:
(1) unchanged learning example plus explicitly consumed named current-value inputs;
also assert the exact unchanged learning decisions in the short oracle case;
(2) existing one-hour rolling-average form over a named spot binding;
(3) existing one-second inner average composed with outer average/change forms.
Reuse existing JSON grammar and expected controlled results; record exact generated
JSON, nodes, bindings, admitted markets and history bytes, not just graph names.
Provide controlled prehistory through public SourceState/evaluator events before
measurement, matching the hour/composed fixtures; record synthetic coverage and
lease assumptions explicitly. No production capability/lease is enabled. Preserve
U1–U5 stops in a separate unsupported-capability control which must never produce
a current candidate. Kalshi observation U2 remains unresolved; book replacements
are initialization/resynchronization, not invented confirmations.

Use a separate disposable pair for 30 seconds of warmup per graph, then destroy it.
Fresh measured pairs receive deterministic initial history/setup; record startup
registration/allocation duration separately. Do not carry warmup checkpoint latches
into measured expectations. Map measurement to a full current 15-minute window
with two descriptors and no intentional rollover campaign; historical setup may
advance the logical epoch before that window. Exact epoch/boundary handling must
be asserted before the run, without backdating late evidence. For preseeded history,
the source.rs test seam must add a fixed logical offset to the worker's sampled
clock and test receipt_ms, matching the completed seed frontier; wall-delay probes
still use unshifted Instant. Otherwise starting the worker at elapsed zero after
an hour seed would be backward time. Apply the offset consistently to advance,
connections, invalidation and publication; self-check the first post-seed effect.
After each ladder,
include 60 seconds of quiet timer/advance-only work and report it separately.
One repetition per graph/profile initially; no automatic reruns/tuning. Repetition
and longer stability runs belong in the later frozen contract. Allow about two
hours for the full serial exploration, including setup/builds; early failed gates
may shorten it.

Each producer uses an absolute monotonic deadline `start + ordinal/rate`, never
`completion + interval`. It must not await worker acknowledgment or evaluator
completion before offering the next item. Nonblocking `admit` preserves current
refusal semantics. Do not prequeue the run: generate one bounded frame at a time.
Record scheduled offer time, actual attempt/receipt time and producer lateness;
if late, keep original deadlines and count every due offer/refusal, with periodic
cancellation checks. No coordinated-omission shortcut that silently slows the
workload. A generator that cannot maintain its declared schedule makes that
attempt incomplete; its late/not-attempted work stays in the denominator.

### Measurements, correctness and failure visibility

Use monotonic nanoseconds for local delays; engine milliseconds and provider UTC
remain separate facts. Define receipt at synthetic raw handoff before memory copy,
not decoder entry. Record scheduled-offer→receipt, receipt→raw-queue admission,
receipt→SourceState apply, receipt→successful `Evaluator::begin` (the normalized
admission target), receipt→relevant `SliceResult::Complete`, and receipt→published
completed-result handoff. A multi-transaction frame gives each member the same
receipt, and each its actual admission/completion. Pure heartbeats/duplicates have
no invented relevant evaluation latency. Also report timer due→completed evaluation.

At each boundary reconcile transactions **and** bytes: offered unique/control/
duplicate frames, raw admitted, decoded, normalized admitted, completed,
duplicate-suppressed, rejected by reason/stage, invalidated, pending, not attempted
and lost/unexplained. Categories are staged (admitted and later invalidated can
overlap), with a disjoint final disposition per identity. Wire bytes for a batch
are charged once at frame level; member wire-byte attribution uses a declared
partition summing exactly to that frame. Normalized bytes use actual batch ingress
accounting. Zero-effect control, duplicate and rejected frames remain visible.
Compare independent generator totals/identities with observed worker and evaluator
counters; do not infer offered counts from the consumer.

Report p50/p95/p99/max for each stage, sample counts and missing/late counts beside
every percentile. **P99 means 99 out of 100 measured completions were at or below
that delay; it says nothing by itself about work that never completed.** Investigate
5-ms p99 normalized admission and 10-ms p99 simple completed evaluation/handoff;
these are exploratory targets, never established capacity, freshness leases or
all-graph guarantees. Report both completion-only percentiles and all-offered
coverage; unresolved/failed work cannot be labeled meeting a target. Use bounded
fixed histograms with declared resolution (e.g. 10 microseconds through 20 ms,
then logarithmic buckets), conservative upper-bound percentiles, separate exact
max and overflow counts. Never cap/drop long samples or allocate a vector per event.

Track actual raw queue depth/high-water, worker/evaluator pending identities and
oldest pending age independently of completed-sample arrays; sample once per second
and on rejection/stop. Report accumulated backlog/drain duration and per-minute
memory/time-series slopes/plateau, not just averages. Probe `Memory::used()` at
reserve/release, raw ownership, decoder scratch/replacement and publication peaks;
after-the-fact snapshot sampling alone can miss simultaneous ownership. Proposed
minimal cfg(test) peak probe in `providers/memory.rs:Memory::reserve` is allowed
only if those transient charges cannot be observed at the source seam; record its
small diff and ordinary reserve/refusal regression. It changes no reservation rule.
Record evaluator `allocated_bytes`, `AdvanceBatch::ingress_bytes`, private metadata
admission outcome, two book charges, three producer payload slots, raw queue/worker,
retained view, fixed structs and measurement memory separately. No per-message
retained ledger: use rolling identity digests, totals and bounded failure examples.

Use installed `/usr/bin/time -l` for process peak RSS/CPU and existing libc/platform
process metrics for one-second CPU/RSS samples. Do not confuse these with payload
charges: allocator/TLS/kernel/OS costs differ. A native test-only System allocator
probe, following the existing engine heap-probe pattern, may count allocation
calls/bytes across owned test threads if needed for allocation-rate reporting;
keep counters allocation-free, include realloc/dealloc and test balanced ownership.
Do not enable the engine's private test probes via a production feature. If this
probe cannot be made faithful in this bounded slice, mark allocation rate missing
and defer it to qualification; charged growth is not a substitute for allocator
rate. No new dependency/instrumentation platform is authorized.

Measure the clock/histogram/atomic overhead with a bounded self-check, record
sampling cadence and instrumentation memory; run one short identical instrumented
versus timing-disabled comparison after approval. Do not subtract estimated
measurement cost from reported latency or call a native cfg(test) executable a
packaged production benchmark. Any material perturbation is a result/limit.

Independent correctness checks use hand-authored expected identity/count/decision
cases in addition to a serial public-interface replay. Include two equal-price
unique spot trades, an exact replay, and a brief true→false→true excursion inside
a four-member batch. Assert observations/checkpoint latches, side/candidate,
historical coverage and final frontier, not only final price. Compare the complete
relevant decision projection/digest after each admitted effect and assert selected
transition decisions literally; do not build the oracle from measured outputs.
Quiet timers add no observations. Keep unsupported history/current controls
unavailable. If synthetic trusted coverage/leases are used for the controlled
history case, publish that assumption beside results; it resolves no provider gap.

On overflow, stale token, decoder/capacity/age failure or evaluator rejection,
record the failed stage and affected identities; revoke/propagate invalidation
before another ordinary batch or completion can appear current. Capture the full
decision dependency stamp and recheck it at handoff. Drain one owned evaluator
batch before another ordinary effect; poll stop between slices. Unexpected Busy
stops the pair, as the existing contract requires. Never continue with guessed
coverage or conceal an invalidated candidate in completed-only statistics.

The small non-ignored self-check must intentionally stall the consumer, force a
queue refusal and one outstanding/late completion, then prove: offered schedule
continues, missing samples fail the target accounting, invalidation makes the
old stamp unusable, exact bytes/counts reconcile, and all handles/charges return.
Corrupt one expected identity or omit one timing sample and assert the report
cannot say complete/pass. Include the equal-price/excursion oracle and histogram
overflow/percentile-rank boundary. Demonstrate these assertions detect the deliberate
fault, not just exercise the reporting code. A later exploratory report says
complete/failed/incomplete with target comparisons; it never says qualified.

trades but omitted the zero-rate/ten-second schedule boundary; passing it did not
establish the quiet fixture. This is a bug introduced in the new harness, not
evidence that Metten invented a provider tick. Do not use this quiet attempt as
quiet-timer/resource acceptance.

Original source establishes two distinct mechanisms:

1. `mod.rs:intake/admit` has one raw slot and immediately revokes the provider
   fence when nonblocking `try_send` fails. `offer_schedule` schedules a Kalshi
   book, trade and BRTI frame at the same initial deadline, then Coinbase and a
   four-trade Kraken frame at 0.1/0.2 ms offsets. The full initial schedule is
   **five frames/eight price transactions** in 0.2 ms; only seven transactions
   were actually attempted before the second Kalshi admission refused and ended
   that producer. This explains the observed seven-versus-eight distinction.
   All required observations must be retained; delaying the replay on completion
   or deleting coincident inputs would hide the overload.
2. `source.rs:start_sources` processes at most one raw item and then unconditionally
   sleeps five milliseconds. Thus even ignoring all processing cost, its long-run
   service upper bound is 200 raw frames/second. The approved 1,000-transaction
   profile offers 636 ordinary raw frames/second (21 Kalshi, 491 Coinbase,
   124 Kraken), plus periodic duplicates. Increasing buffering alone cannot make
   that sustained schedule fit; a queue-only fix would postpone refusal.
3. `SourceWorker::new` starts its monotonic epoch **before** setup feeds the
   controlled history through the evaluator and reference replay. The first
   controlled market opens at logical offset +1,000 ms. At worker start the source
   samples offset +elapsed wall time since that earlier epoch, and `advance`
   delivers the prepared boundary at its scheduled opening. The timer probe uses
   the same early epoch + (batch target -offset) for delay. Consequently history
   setup/catch-up elapsed time can enter the clock histogram. This establishes
   a concrete contamination mechanism for the 8.53-second maximum, not a measured
   8.53-second steady-state evaluator service time. Existing samples lack phase
   tags, so the exact attribution of all three long samples remains unproved.

pub fn intake() -> (mpsc::Sender<Intake>, mpsc::Receiver<Intake>) { mpsc::channel(1) }
pub fn admit(sender:&mpsc::Sender<Intake>,fence:&Fence,item:Intake)->Result<(),Failure> {
 if !Arc::ptr_eq(&fence.generation,&item.fence.generation)||!fence.current(item.generation){fence.reject();return Err(Failure::Stopped);}
 if item.bytes.len()>MAX_BYTES {fence.revoke();return Err(Failure::Capacity);}
 sender.try_send(item).map_err(|_|{fence.revoke();Failure::Capacity})
}

### Necessary simultaneous-ownership correction identified before qualification

The C3 synthetic no-socket workload is not full topology qualification: three
socket reservations consume12MiB. At10 Kalshi trades/s for900s, unchanged
id-length+2048 charges alone consume over17.6MiB, plus two books4.125MiB and
scratch4MiB. Thus that original reservation policy cannot support the declared
15-minute topology within32MiB even if intake is infinitely fast. It is not safe
to call no-socket success full capacity. No cap increase or identity eviction is
allowed. Expected correction path expands locally to Kalshi's existing retained
trade ledger and covering decoder/resource tests, plus affected contract/evidence.
This is a current required capacity correction, not unrelated cleanup.

Reused unchanged Rust1.100.0 compiler-layout evidence from issue4, independently
reread cached exact compiler node.rs at0ef1bc386059596dada8fb65b50425aab2ea637a:
11 keys/12 edges, minimum5 non-root keys. String key24B and ledger value
(i128,i128,OwnedSemaphorePermit) bounded64B give internal-node allowance
128+11*(24+64)=1096B, rounded conservatively to1152B. Nodes<=1+floor((N-1)/5).
Retain2048B for first identity/root and512B for each later identity, plus each
owned text length. This dominates1152*(1+floor((N-1)/5)) at every N>=1, including
root/split growth before insertion completes; no replacement ledger is cloned.
Outer two-ledger roots/ticker strings remain in the existing64KiB native base.
Add literal type-size asserts and allocator/retention/cap-refusal checks before
accepting this tighter reservation. Reconnect/duplicate/conflict/retirement behavior
must remain unchanged; all identities remain retained. C3 executable remains
unchanged and its exploration remains no-socket evidence, not this correction.

The ledger derivation permits256B per later identity (1152/5=230.4B;256 is the
next ordinary alignment multiple with headroom), retaining2048B for the root.
The preliminary512B value was deliberately conservative and was checked in the
10,000-identity allocator/retention/refusal self-check;256B is the derived candidate
before full-topology exploration, not a changed qualification threshold. General
inequality:2048+256*(N-1) >=1152*(1+floor((N-1)/5)), N>=1. Text remains additional.
The exact short check retains10,000 identities, validates actual live Rust heap
against charges+existing64KiB base, replays the first identity without observation,
rejects a conflicting first identity, forces shared-byte exhaustion and verifies
all permits release on drop. A temporary wrong Event module import was corrected
before tests; the512B focused check passed.256B and full topology remain unverified.

Final accounting audit before freeze found two failure-only inaccuracies. Transaction length included validity/gap/boundary effects as prices when associated with a failed raw frame. Price counters/histograms now count only transactions containing Observation or Resynchronize; non-price normalized/completed control transactions have distinct counters and still reach both evaluators unchanged.             h = r["latency"][name]
```python
            if set(h) != {"count","max_ns","over_20ms","p50_upper_ns","p95_upper_ns","p99_upper_ns"}: return False
            if not all(type(h[k]) is int and h[k] >= 0 for k in ["count","max_ns","over_20ms"]): return False
            if not all((h[k] is None if h["count"] == 0 else type(h[k]) is int and h[k] >= 0) for k in ["p50_upper_ns","p95_upper_ns","p99_upper_ns"]): return False
        for key in ["rss_cpu_start","rss_cpu_end"]:
            v = r["resources"][key]
            if not isinstance(v,list) or len(v)!=3 or not all(type(n) is int and n>=0 for n in v): return False
        return True
    except (KeyError,TypeError,ValueError): return False

def identity():
    assert hashlib.sha256(EXECUTABLE.read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="2b1333e2de43c5460c20282c47da0892fc41781d6ce058e46947a771a9ada513", "executable changed"
    manifest = "".join(hashlib.sha256((ROOT/p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()+"  "+p+"\n" for p in SOURCE_FILES)
    assert hashlib.sha256(manifest.encode()).hexdigest()=="a858d17df2f2ea23bcb37ea3830b4a2af67f8f898bd62585b1fddff0326ae2b7", "source changed"
    assert hashlib.sha256((ROOT/"docs/sources/performance.md").read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="0ec3a2904ef006fd08a9f36c9661d9f1e429b17a15560d9b997f4cf13a740412", "contract changed"

def negative_checks(path):
    reports = [json.loads(l[12:]) for l in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if l.startswith("CALIBRATION {")]
    assert len(reports)==3
    for r in reports:
        assert shape(r)
        for section, keys in [("counts",COUNT_KEYS),("bytes",BYTE_KEYS),("resources",RESOURCE_KEYS)]:
            for key in keys:
                omitted=copy.deepcopy(r); del omitted[section][key]
                assert not shape(omitted), (section,key)
        for name in HISTOGRAMS:
            omitted=copy.deepcopy(r); del omitted["latency"][name]["count"]
            assert not shape(omitted), name
    identity()
    print("PREQUALIFICATION_COMPLETENESS passed: all required field/sample omissions rejected")

def check(path):
    identity()
    text=Path(path).read_text(); reports=[]; offers=[]; verdicts=[]
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("CALIBRATION {"):
            reports.append(json.loads(line[12:])); offers.append([])
        elif line.startswith("CALIBRATION offers "):
            assert offers, "orphan provider disposition"
            provider=int(re.search(r"provider=(\d+)",line).group(1))
            values={k:int(re.search(r"\b"+k+r": (\d+)",line).group(1)) for k in ["attempted","admitted","transactions","admitted_transactions","bytes","admitted_bytes","late","max_lateness_ns"]}
            offers[-1].append((provider,values))
        elif line.startswith("QUALIFICATION "):
            verdicts.append(json.loads(line[14:]))
    profiles=[("warmup",100,30),("low",100,900),("medium",1000,900),("burst",10000,1),("quiet",0,60)]
    expected=[(g,label,rate,seconds) for g in range(3) for label,rate,seconds in profiles]
    assert len(reports)==len(verdicts)==len(offers)==15, "missing case/report/verdict"
    for r,v,oo,(g,label,rate,seconds) in zip(reports,verdicts,offers,expected):
        assert (r["graph"],r["case"],r["rate"],r["duration_s"])==(g,label,rate,seconds)
        assert r["qualification"] is True and shape(r), (g,label,"missing required telemetry")
        assert (v["graph"],v["case"],v["contract"],v["passed"])==(g,label,"issue-5-step-6-v1",True), (g,label,"native qualification gate failed")
        assert [p for p,_ in oo]==[0,1,2], (g,label,"missing provider dispositions")
        c,b=r["counts"],r["bytes"]
        for offered,section,key in [("attempted",c,"offered_frames"),("admitted",c,"raw_admitted_frames"),("transactions",c,"attempted_unique"),("admitted_transactions",c,"raw_admitted_unique"),("bytes",b,"offered_wire"),("admitted_bytes",b,"raw_admitted_wire")]:
            assert sum(o[offered] for _,o in oo)==section[key], (g,label,offered)
        assert all(o["late"]<=o["attempted"] for _,o in oo)
        if rate<=100:
            assert all(o["max_lateness_ns"]<=100_000_000 for _,o in oo), (g,label,"supported offer lateness exceeded")
    def os_value(label):
        m=re.search(r"^\s*(\d+)\s+"+re.escape(label)+r"$",text,re.M)
        assert m, "missing OS "+label
        return int(m.group(1))
    rss=os_value("maximum resident set size"); footprint=os_value("peak memory footprint"); swaps=os_value("swaps")
    assert rss<=256*1024*1024 and footprint<=256*1024*1024 and swaps==0, "OS resource contract failed"
    assert "test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed;" in text, "native process did not pass"
    print(json.dumps({"contract":"issue-5-step-6-v1","qualified":True,"cases":15,"provider_dispositions":45,"os_max_rss_bytes":rss,"os_peak_footprint_bytes":footprint,"swaps":swaps,"log_sha256":hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()},sort_keys=True))

if __name__=="__main__":
    if sys.argv[1]=="--self-check": negative_checks(sys.argv[2])
    else: check(sys.argv[1])
```

## Fixed workload

Run all five cases once for each graph0/1/2, serially in that order. Each case has
fresh owned sockets/source/evaluators/workspace and a one-second post-seed startup.
The separate30-second warmup precedes the measured low case in the same process;
it does not carry source state into that fresh case. Setup/history initialization
is separate from measured clock/receipt timing.

| Case | Combined price transactions/s | Nominal offer duration | Expected unique prices | Raw frames | Raw bytes if fully offered |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warmup | 100 | 30s | 3,000 | 2,192 | 1,414,144 |
| Supported low | 100 | 900s | 90,000 | 65,789 | 44,532,224 |
| Medium stress | 1,000 | 900s | 900,000 | 572,489 | 356,033,024 |
| Burst stress | 10,000 | 1s | 10,000 | 6,261 | 4,372,480 |
| Quiet | 0 | 60s | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The proposed supported envelope requires all100/s cases and quiet cases to pass
for all three graphs. Medium/burst are outside that declared envelope: either
complete exactly or demonstrate the fixed explicit-refusal safety contract below.
Their nominal remaining work after refusal is unattempted, never counted as
completed or as proof of sustained capacity. No lower rate, shorter historical
window, smoothed schedule or observation removal can substitute for a failed100/s case.

Graph0 is the learning-derived current-value graph with all bound price inputs,
equal-price-confirmation and excursion checkpoints. Graph1 adds a3,600-second
Coinbase rolling average; graph2 adds a one-second average followed by a one-second
change. Their exact validated JSON hashes are printed in each manifest. Controlled
initial frontiers are0/3,600,001/2,001ms respectively, with complete seeded history.
Test-only contiguous accepted-time quiet coverage renews through SourceState only
while its original Coinbase fence/initialization/proof is valid. This adds no price
observations, repairs no gaps and establishes no upstream U3 guarantee. Leases and
metadata are explicit synthetic trust inputs. Two prepared15-minute markets are
retained; a900-second offer window plus post-offer grace crosses the successor boundary.

Every second offers nine1,024-byte book snapshots, ten512-byte Kalshi trades,
**one512-byte BRTI tick**, and three512-byte control/heartbeat frames. Coinbase and
Kraken each supply40/490/4,990 price transactions per second at the three rates;
Coinbase uses one512-byte frame/transaction, Kraken batches up to four in1,024B.
Ordinary raw rates are73/636/6,261 frames/s. A512-byte Coinbase replay occurs at
second10,20,... below the case duration, at850ms within that second. Controls occur
at900ms. Provider phase offsets are0/100/200 microseconds. The first book snapshot
at seconds60,300,600,840 becomes512KiB; burst's first book is512KiB. No new BRTI ticks
or meaningful observations are manufactured. Full schedule enumeration includes
control/replay/phase alignment and second boundaries; worst five-ms arrival counts
are6/8/36. Eight slots is not a guarantee against arbitrary OS/service pauses.

Each producer retains absolute monotonic deadlines and awaits only its own real
loopback send/receive, never source/evaluator completion. Late deadlines catch up
without rescheduling; per-provider late-count/max are retained. All supported offers
must have maximum lateness <=100ms (checked from all provider disposition records).
Frame-to-local-receipt is separate from receipt-to-source/engine/publication.
Offers end at the nominal deadline; the driver allows at least100ms post-offer grace
and reports its actual duration. No additional price offers occur during grace.

Native contention stays enabled: local SourceView serialization approximately once
per second with a4MiB response reservation, validated learning-strategy preview and
immutable save plus a256KiB diagnostic rewrite/sync at most once per ten seconds.
Each blocking operation is joined. Require view reads between90% of nominal seconds
and seconds+2, and saves between floor(seconds/11) and floor(seconds/10)+1 for supported
cases. Missed secondary ticks skip catch-up; price offers never use that policy.

## Fixed correctness and accounting gates

Supported cases require every expected price normalized, admitted, primarily completed,
reference-verified, active with required history complete, identity-checked and handed
off current. Exact frame/byte totals must also match. Require zero rejection,
unattempted work, pending/canceled work, invalidated completion, decoder error or
unexplained loss. Genuine completed transactions equal prices minus(9*seconds+4),
resynchronizations equal9*seconds+4, and suppressed replay frames equal floor((seconds-1)/10)
for positive-rate cases. Quiet has zero price work/replay and no unexpected BRTI input.
Require initial boundary plus successor boundary for900-second cases (two); other
cases have one. Boundary completion/publication/identity counts must match with no
invalidated handoff. Every decision equals an independent public Evaluator replay.

Price transactions contain Observation or Resynchronize. Validity/gap/boundary
transactions are counted separately and still processed. Normalization, engine
admission, primary completion, reference verification and publication are distinct.
Primary completion is recorded before reference replay, so failed verification
cannot erase it. Every frame/transaction/byte funnel must balance, including socket
failure, raw refusal, admission refusal, cancellation, rejection and invalidation.
All cases, including overload, require all histograms and exact stage sample counts.
Deliberately omitted completed counts or admission samples must prevent a pass.

The ordinary/release focused checks also require literal controlled decisions,
equal-price genuine observations, suppressed replay, brief excursions, consistent
post-seed frontier/time, pending Stop/invalidation, stale-view refusal, capacity+one,
byte exhaustion/permit release, no per-frame idle delay and no OS/report operation
under the queue-accounting mutex. The exact one-MiB/8,192-levels-per-side real-socket
case asserts six frames/nine transactions/1,052,160B and89.991809-cent resulting ask.
A failed reference preserves primary completed1/verified0/invalidated1/handoff0.

## Fixed delay limits

The delay gates in this table apply to the supported warmup/100/s/quiet cases.
Stress-case tails remain fully reported and use the overload safety bounds below.
All numbers below are milliseconds. Quantiles use10-microsecond upper bins through
20ms plus an uncapped overflow maximum. Every expected price/frame must supply its
sample; a fast subset cannot meet a target. Primary completion excludes later
reference replay; publication includes that real CPU/publication overhead.

| Stage | Graphs | p50 <= | p95 <= | p99 <= | max <= |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Offer → local receipt | All | 1 | 3 | 5 | 100 |
| Receipt → source / normalized engine admission | Current | 2.5 | 5 | 5 | 100 |
| Receipt → primary completion | Current | 3 | 6 | 10 | 100 |
| Receipt → current publication | Current | 4 | 8 | 10 | 100 |
| Receipt → source / normalized engine admission | Historical | 3 | 8 | 10 | 100 |
| Receipt → primary completion | Historical | 4 | 10 | 15 | 100 |
| Receipt → current publication | Historical | 5 | 12 | 20 | 100 |
| Sampled clock target → completion | All | 2 | 3 | 5 | 100 |
| Synthetic coverage target → completion | Historical | 2 | 4 | 6 | 100 |
| Startup clock target → completion | All | 3 | 10 | 20 | 100 |
| Scheduled boundary → completion/publication | All | 10 | 10 | 10 | 50 |

Require100–4,000 measured clock completions/nominal second; historical coverage has
at least100 completions/second, current graphs none. Startup has nonzero separate
samples. Oldest pending/processing age max100ms in the supported cases. The small
boundary sample count means its p99 effectively checks every measured handoff;
no claim about a population distribution follows.

The current-value5/10ms admission/completion p99 targets preserve the approved
exploration points. Historical10/15/20ms admission/completion/publication targets
reflect their greater measured processing cost (C5/C6 short history p99 roughly
6–8ms) with declared headroom. Max100ms and resource bounds retain finite tails;
C5 historical refusals still fail this contract regardless of favorable percentiles.
No qualification outcome selected these limits.

## Fixed resource and overload gates

- Eight raw slots, two-second raw age refusal and the unchanged shared32MiB adapter
  payload allowance. All reservations precede growth; more slots grant no bytes.
  One-MiB messages, depth48,16KiB text,128B identities,8,192 levels/side,two books,
  existing replacement limits and256KiB views remain. No automatic cap escalation.
- Per-evaluator accounted peaks <=8,388,608 /65,988,608 /8,420,624B for graphs0/1/2.
  One-hour history is additional to the existing8MiB non-history allowance;
  primary and reference evaluators own separate histories. Existing4,096 slice/
  ingress/resource proofs and financial/arithmetic/storage semantics remain.
- Mean process-wide Rust allocation calls (including reallocation/zeroed calls,
  fixtures, reference and harness) <=2,000,000/s through joined shutdown; setup is
  separately counted/timed and <=60s. This is a measured call-rate bound, not an
  allocation-free hot-path claim. Rust frees/live requested bytes and per-sample
  cumulative allocation counts are retained. OS/TLS/C allocations are outside that
  counter and visible only where the OS measurements include them.
- Supported mean CPU (user+system tuple delta / observed wall) <=0.8 of one CPU core.
  All-case sampled RSS <=256MiB, sampled Rust live requested bytes <=192MiB, final
  requested live bytes <=4MiB. Supported steady sampled live-byte range after5s
  <=8MiB, allowing bounded trade-ID/book growth through a market; raw highwater <=8.
  Independently require whole-process OS maximum RSS **and** peak footprint <=256MiB,
  zero swaps, from `/usr/bin/time -l`. Setup/reference/harness cost remains included.
- All owned provider/socket/source/storage work must join. Shutdown <=5s; adapter
  charges must return to zero after dropping retained handles/views. Engine stops
  and joins its recorder before removing only its mode0700 disposable workspace.
  No stop request or green process exit substitutes for those assertions.
- Medium/burst must either complete all exact work or return explicit capacity
  refusal with <=500ms first-refusal-to-driver detection, revoked affected fences
  and an unusable retained aggregate view **before Stop**. Require balanced complete
  dispositions, zero unexplained loss, oldest recorded pending age <=2s and joined
  cleanup under the same resource ceilings. A transport/control/processing error or
  missing evidence is not an accepted capacity refusal. No sustained higher-rate
  capacity claim follows from a safety pass.

Simultaneous adapter inventory includes three4MiB socket/task reservations, up to
three producer-held bodies, eight queued bodies and one processing body,4MiB decode
scratch,two books4,325,376B/replacement overlap6,488,064B,64KiB native base, retained
views and4MiB response work, plus bounded controls/HTTP/metadata allowances. Trade
ledgers retain every opaque identity:2048B root/first identity,256B later entry plus
ID bytes under the pinned B-tree/isolated allocator proof. These individual maxima
cannot all coexist under32MiB; refusal is required. SourceState/evaluators, reference,
probe, fixture generation and platform/allocator/kernel costs have distinct ownership.
`Memory::peak` is an observed lower bound under concurrent release, not an exact
transient peak proof; the semaphore/general ownership argument establishes the cap.
The process/Rust bounds above do not redefine adapter charge as RSS.

## Fixed workload

Run all five cases once for each graph0/1/2, serially in that order. Each case has
fresh owned sockets/source/evaluators/workspace and a one-second post-seed startup.
The separate30-second warmup precedes the measured low case in the same process;
it does not carry source state into that fresh case. Setup/history initialization
is separate from measured clock/receipt timing.

| Case | Combined price transactions/s | Nominal offer duration | Expected unique prices | Raw frames | Raw bytes if fully offered |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Warmup | 100 | 30s | 3,000 | 2,192 | 1,414,144 |
| Supported low | 100 | 900s | 90,000 | 65,789 | 44,532,224 |
| Medium stress | 1,000 | 900s | 900,000 | 572,489 | 356,033,024 |
| Burst stress | 10,000 | 1s | 10,000 | 6,261 | 4,372,480 |
| Quiet | 0 | 60s | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The proposed supported envelope requires all100/s cases and quiet cases to pass
for all three graphs. Medium/burst are outside that declared envelope: either
complete exactly or demonstrate the fixed explicit-refusal safety contract below.
Their nominal remaining work after refusal is unattempted, never counted as
completed or as proof of sustained capacity. No lower rate, shorter historical
window, smoothed schedule or observation removal can substitute for a failed100/s case.

Graph0 is the learning-derived current-value graph with all bound price inputs,
equal-price-confirmation and excursion checkpoints. Graph1 adds a3,600-second
Coinbase rolling average; graph2 adds a one-second average followed by a one-second
change. Their exact validated JSON hashes are printed in each manifest. Controlled
initial frontiers are0/3,600,001/2,001ms respectively, with complete seeded history.
Test-only contiguous accepted-time quiet coverage renews through SourceState only
while its original Coinbase fence/initialization/proof is valid. This adds no price
observations, repairs no gaps and establishes no upstream U3 guarantee. Leases and
metadata are explicit synthetic trust inputs. Two prepared15-minute markets are
retained; a900-second offer window plus post-offer grace crosses the successor boundary.

Every second offers nine1,024-byte book snapshots, ten512-byte Kalshi trades,
**one512-byte BRTI tick**, and three512-byte control/heartbeat frames. Coinbase and
Kraken each supply40/490/4,990 price transactions per second at the three rates;
Coinbase uses one512-byte frame/transaction, Kraken batches up to four in1,024B.
Ordinary raw rates are73/636/6,261 frames/s. A512-byte Coinbase replay occurs at
second10,20,... below the case duration, at850ms within that second. Controls occur
at900ms. Provider phase offsets are0/100/200 microseconds. The first book snapshot
at seconds60,300,600,840 becomes512KiB; burst's first book is512KiB. No new BRTI ticks
or meaningful observations are manufactured. Full schedule enumeration includes
control/replay/phase alignment and second boundaries; worst five-ms arrival counts
are6/8/36. Eight slots is not a guarantee against arbitrary OS/service pauses.

Each producer retains absolute monotonic deadlines and awaits only its own real
loopback send/receive, never source/evaluator completion. Late deadlines catch up
without rescheduling; per-provider late-count/max are retained. All supported offers
must have maximum lateness <=100ms (checked from all provider disposition records).
Frame-to-local-receipt is separate from receipt-to-source/engine/publication.
Offers end at the nominal deadline; the driver allows at least100ms post-offer grace
and reports its actual duration. No additional price offers occur during grace.

Native contention stays enabled: local SourceView serialization approximately once
per second with a4MiB response reservation, validated learning-strategy preview and
immutable save plus a256KiB diagnostic rewrite/sync at most once per ten seconds.
Each blocking operation is joined. Require view reads between90% of nominal seconds
and seconds+2, and saves between floor(seconds/11) and floor(seconds/10)+1 for supported
cases. Missed secondary ticks skip catch-up; price offers never use that policy.

## Fixed correctness and accounting gates

Supported cases require every expected price normalized, admitted, primarily completed,
reference-verified, active with required history complete, identity-checked and handed
off current. Exact frame/byte totals must also match. Require zero rejection,
unattempted work, pending/canceled work, invalidated completion, decoder error or
unexplained loss. Genuine completed transactions equal prices minus(9*seconds+4),
resynchronizations equal9*seconds+4, and suppressed replay frames equal floor((seconds-1)/10)
for positive-rate cases. Quiet has zero price work/replay and no unexpected BRTI input.
Require initial boundary plus successor boundary for900-second cases (two); other
cases have one. Boundary completion/publication/identity counts must match with no
invalidated handoff. Every decision equals an independent public Evaluator replay.

Price transactions contain Observation or Resynchronize. Validity/gap/boundary
transactions are counted separately and still processed. Normalization, engine
admission, primary completion, reference verification and publication are distinct.
Primary completion is recorded before reference replay, so failed verification
cannot erase it. Every frame/transaction/byte funnel must balance, including socket
failure, raw refusal, admission refusal, cancellation, rejection and invalidation.
All cases, including overload, require all histograms and exact stage sample counts.
Deliberately omitted completed counts or admission samples must prevent a pass.

The ordinary/release focused checks also require literal controlled decisions,
equal-price genuine observations, suppressed replay, brief excursions, consistent
post-seed frontier/time, pending Stop/invalidation, stale-view refusal, capacity+one,
byte exhaustion/permit release, no per-frame idle delay and no OS/report operation
under the queue-accounting mutex. The exact one-MiB/8,192-levels-per-side real-socket
case asserts six frames/nine transactions/1,052,160B and89.991809-cent resulting ask.
A failed reference preserves primary completed1/verified0/invalidated1/handoff0.

C9 measurement borrows the actual published SourceView, keeps queue counters separate
from OS queries/formatting, and tests the retained pre-offer view on refusal. It skips
only an identical already-completed empty evaluator clock at the same frontier,
watermark and admission; all new times/admission/price/control/coverage run normally.
Those suppressed requests are counted separately, never as completion samples.
Private coverage reuses the worker's correct-time snapshot, refreshing after a
boundary. All SourceWorker checks/publications still run; source/handle/probe clocks
share the post-seed origin and retain their completed logical offsets.

## Fixed delay limits

The delay gates in this table apply to the supported warmup/100/s/quiet cases.

  existing replacement limits and256KiB views remain. No automatic cap escalation.

  One-hour history is additional to the existing8MiB non-history allowance;
  primary and reference evaluators own separate histories. Existing4,096 slice/
  ingress/resource proofs and financial/arithmetic/storage semantics remain.
- Mean process-wide Rust allocation calls (including reallocation/zeroed calls,
  fixtures, reference and harness) <=2,000,000/s through joined shutdown; setup is
  separately counted/timed and <=60s. This is a measured call-rate bound, not an
  allocation-free hot-path claim. Rust frees/live requested bytes and per-sample
  cumulative allocation counts are retained. OS/TLS/C allocations are outside that
  counter and visible only where the OS measurements include them.
- Supported mean CPU (user+system tuple delta / observed wall) <=0.8 of one CPU core.
  All-case sampled RSS <=256MiB, sampled Rust live requested bytes <=192MiB, final
  requested live bytes <=4MiB. Supported steady sampled live-byte range after5s
  <=8MiB, allowing bounded trade-ID/book growth through a market; raw highwater <=8.
  Independently require whole-process OS maximum RSS **and** peak footprint <=256MiB,
  zero swaps, from `/usr/bin/time -l`. Setup/reference/harness cost remains included.
- All owned provider/socket/source/storage work must join. Shutdown <=5s; adapter
  charges must return to zero after dropping retained handles/views. Engine stops
  and joins its recorder before removing only its mode0700 disposable workspace.
  No stop request or green process exit substitutes for those assertions.
  Per-case observed resource windows end after source/socket joins. Whole-process
  OS measurements also cover the final Engine stop/recorder join/directory removal.
  Serial non-overlapping case windows permit a conservative cleanup check: subtract
  summed setup/observed wall from OS real time, then add all remaining process gaps
  and0.02s OS rounding margin to maximum measured source shutdown; require that
  combined upper bound <=5s as well. No final cleanup is silently excluded.
- Medium/burst must either complete all exact work or return explicit capacity
  refusal with <=500ms first-refusal-to-driver detection, revoked affected fences

  dispositions, zero unexplained loss, oldest recorded pending age <=2s and joined
  cleanup under the same resource ceilings. A transport/control/processing error or
  missing evidence is not an accepted capacity refusal. No sustained higher-rate

```python
BYTE_KEYS = frozenset(['canceled_before_worker_wire', 'consumer_wire', 'decode_rejected_wire', 'decoded_wire', 'expected_wire', 'ingress_peak', 'not_attempted_wire', 'offered_wire', 'raw_admitted_wire', 'raw_refused_wire', 'socket_failed_wire', 'socket_received_wire'])
RESOURCE_KEYS = frozenset(['resource_query_calls', 'resource_query_total_ns', 'resource_query_max_ns', 'suppressed_identical_empty_clocks', 'adapter_peak', 'allocation_calls_including_harness', 'allocation_observation_wall_s', 'bounded_diagnostic_bytes', 'deallocation_calls_including_harness', 'engine_accounted_peak', 'native_view_reads', 'oldest_pending_age_max_ns', 'probe_inline_bytes', 'processing_canceled_receipt', 'queued_canceled_frames', 'raw_highwater', 'reference_engine_accounted_peak', 'rss_cpu_end', 'rss_cpu_start', 'rust_live_bytes_including_harness', 'sampled_live_peak_including_harness', 'sampled_rss_peak', 'setup_allocation_calls', 'setup_ns', 'shutdown_ns', 'steady_sampled_live_range', 'strategy_preview_saves'])
HISTOGRAMS = ['admission', 'boundary_completion', 'boundary_publication', 'completion', 'offered_frame_to_loopback_receipt', 'publication', 'sampled_clock_to_complete', 'source', 'startup_clock_to_complete', 'synthetic_coverage_to_complete']
ROOT = Path('/Users/connormoulton/.t3/worktrees/metten/t3-5ff0c48e-8b502ba4b606ca11')
EXECUTABLE = ROOT / "target/release/build/metten/64aabbdc086925d0/out/metten-64aabbdc086925d0"
SOURCE_FILES = ["crates/engine/src/sources.rs", "crates/engine/tests/sources.rs"] + ["src-tauri/src/providers/"+n+".rs" for n in ["mod","memory","source","tests","kalshi","transport"]]
OFFER_KEYS = ["attempted", "admitted", "transactions", "admitted_transactions", "bytes", "admitted_bytes", "late", "max_lateness_ns", "max_timer_overrun_ns", "max_carryover_lateness_ns", "max_intake_lock_wait_ns"]
def provider_fields(line):
    values = {}
    for k in OFFER_KEYS:
        match = re.search(r"\b"+k+r": (\d+)", line)
        if match is None: return None
        values[k] = int(match.group(1))
    if any(values[k] > values["max_lateness_ns"] for k in ["max_timer_overrun_ns", "max_carryover_lateness_ns"]): return None
    return values

def shape(r):
    try:
        if set(r["counts"]) != COUNT_KEYS or set(r["bytes"]) != BYTE_KEYS or set(r["resources"]) != RESOURCE_KEYS: return False
        if not all(type(v) is int and v >= 0 for section in ["counts","bytes"] for v in r[section].values()): return False
        q = r["resources"]
        if not all(type(q[k]) is int and q[k] >= 0 for k in ["resource_query_calls", "resource_query_total_ns", "resource_query_max_ns"]): return False
        if not 2 <= q["resource_query_calls"] <= q["native_view_reads"] + 3: return False
        if q["resource_query_total_ns"] < q["resource_query_max_ns"]: return False
        c = r["counts"]
        if c["non_price_completed_transactions"] > c["non_price_normalized_transactions"]: return False
        for name in HISTOGRAMS:
            h = r["latency"][name]
            if set(h) != {"count","max_ns","over_20ms","p50_upper_ns","p95_upper_ns","p99_upper_ns"}: return False
            if not all(type(h[k]) is int and h[k] >= 0 for k in ["count","max_ns","over_20ms"]): return False
            if not all((h[k] is None if h["count"] == 0 else type(h[k]) is int and h[k] >= 0) for k in ["p50_upper_ns","p95_upper_ns","p99_upper_ns"]): return False
        for key in ["rss_cpu_start","rss_cpu_end"]:
            v = r["resources"][key]
            if not isinstance(v,list) or len(v)!=3 or not all(type(n) is int and n>=0 for n in v): return False
        return True
    except (KeyError,TypeError,ValueError): return False

def identity():
    assert hashlib.sha256(EXECUTABLE.read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="65c1c07a54b976a9cdd5b78afa5e8e2e4045414a458639cbf280476cd6773612", "executable changed"
    manifest = "".join(hashlib.sha256((ROOT/p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()+"  "+p+"\n" for p in SOURCE_FILES)
    assert hashlib.sha256(manifest.encode()).hexdigest()=="77dc1ab9c649443b2b216d203a2474ad4ba63d977f969dc0fb7531098606605a", "source changed"
    assert hashlib.sha256((ROOT/"docs/sources/performance.md").read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="03dc35155b7b3b7a53ce35e0f90231440708078f4e525a3cdef39af87d7585e5", "contract changed"

def negative_checks(path):
    reports = [json.loads(l[12:]) for l in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if l.startswith("CALIBRATION {")]
    assert len(reports)==12
    for r in reports:
        assert shape(r)
        for section, keys in [("counts",COUNT_KEYS),("bytes",BYTE_KEYS),("resources",RESOURCE_KEYS)]:
            for key in keys:
                omitted=copy.deepcopy(r); del omitted[section][key]
                assert not shape(omitted), (section,key)
        for name in HISTOGRAMS:
            omitted=copy.deepcopy(r); del omitted["latency"][name]["count"]
            assert not shape(omitted), name
    lines = [l for l in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if l.startswith("CALIBRATION offers ")]
    assert len(lines) == 36
    for line in lines:
        assert provider_fields(line) is not None
        for key in OFFER_KEYS:
            omitted = re.sub(r"\b"+key+r": \d+,? ?", "", line, count=1)
            assert provider_fields(omitted) is None, key
    identity()
    print("PREQUALIFICATION_COMPLETENESS passed: all required field/sample omissions rejected")

def check(path):
    identity()
    text=Path(path).read_text(); reports=[]; offers=[]; verdicts=[]
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("CALIBRATION {"):
            reports.append(json.loads(line[12:])); offers.append([])
        elif line.startswith("CALIBRATION offers "):
            assert offers, "orphan provider disposition"
            provider=int(re.search(r"provider=(\d+)",line).group(1))
            values=provider_fields(line)
            assert values is not None, "missing/invalid provider phase telemetry"
            offers[-1].append((provider,values))
        elif line.startswith("QUALIFICATION "):
            verdicts.append(json.loads(line[14:]))
    profiles=[("warmup",100,30),("low",100,900),("medium",1000,900),("burst",10000,1),("quiet",0,60)]
    expected=[(g,label,rate,seconds) for g in range(3) for label,rate,seconds in profiles]
    assert len(reports)==len(verdicts)==len(offers)==15, "missing case/report/verdict"
    for r,v,oo,(g,label,rate,seconds) in zip(reports,verdicts,offers,expected):
        assert (r["graph"],r["case"],r["rate"],r["duration_s"])==(g,label,rate,seconds)
        assert r["qualification"] is True and shape(r), (g,label,"missing required telemetry")
        assert (v["graph"],v["case"],v["contract"],v["passed"])==(g,label,"issue-5-step-6-v1",True), (g,label,"native qualification gate failed")
        assert [p for p,_ in oo]==[0,1,2], (g,label,"missing provider dispositions")
        c,b=r["counts"],r["bytes"]
        for offered,section,key in [("attempted",c,"offered_frames"),("admitted",c,"raw_admitted_frames"),("transactions",c,"attempted_unique"),("admitted_transactions",c,"raw_admitted_unique"),("bytes",b,"offered_wire"),("admitted_bytes",b,"raw_admitted_wire")]:
            assert sum(o[offered] for _,o in oo)==section[key], (g,label,offered)
        assert all(o["late"]<=o["attempted"] for _,o in oo)
        if rate<=100:
            assert all(o["max_lateness_ns"]<=100_000_000 for _,o in oo), (g,label,"supported offer lateness exceeded")
    def os_value(label):
        m=re.search(r"^\s*(\d+)\s+"+re.escape(label)+r"$",text,re.M)
        assert m, "missing OS "+label
        return int(m.group(1))
    rss=os_value("maximum resident set size"); footprint=os_value("peak memory footprint"); swaps=os_value("swaps")
    assert rss<=256*1024*1024 and footprint<=256*1024*1024 and swaps==0, "OS resource contract failed"
    assert "test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed;" in text, "native process did not pass"
    m=re.search(r"^\s*(\d+\.\d+) real\s+", text, re.M)
    assert m, "missing OS wall duration"
    observed=sum(r["resources"]["setup_ns"]/1e9+r["resources"]["allocation_observation_wall_s"] for r in reports)
    residual=float(m.group(1))-observed
    assert residual>=-0.02, "per-case observation windows overlap OS duration"
    cleanup_bound=max(r["resources"]["shutdown_ns"] for r in reports)/1e9+max(0,residual)+0.02
    assert cleanup_bound<=5, "combined source/socket/storage cleanup bound exceeded"
    print(json.dumps({"all_unobserved_process_gaps_s":residual,"conservative_combined_cleanup_bound_s":cleanup_bound},sort_keys=True))
    print(json.dumps({"contract":"issue-5-step-6-v1","qualified":True,"cases":15,"provider_dispositions":45,"os_max_rss_bytes":rss,"os_peak_footprint_bytes":footprint,"swaps":swaps,"log_sha256":hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()},sort_keys=True))

if __name__=="__main__":
    if sys.argv[1]=="--self-check": negative_checks(sys.argv[2])
    else: check(sys.argv[1])
```
