### C19 bounded observation, correction and regression

Expected change path: existing mpsc intake notification → existing SourceWorker wait; private Calibration receive retains serialized queue accounting. Affected files are providers/mod.rs, source.rs and tests.rs, plus existing owning contract/map. No new source owner, scheduler, runtime, dependency, capacity or financial semantics. Maintainability references inspected: code map, product specification, ADR0001, glossary, source profiles/U1–U7, native calibration contract, approved design/step2/4/5 plans and performance contract; CONTRIBUTING and SECURITY. Approved proposal hashes remain owner-pinned.

Ranked predictions: an uninterruptible idle timeout produces wall delay without comparable thread CPU; synchronous processing produces delay in advance/decode/evaluation/publication, with CPU distinguishing computation from waiting; measurement interference produces delay correlated with resource/report locks or reference overhead. C19 adds phase boundaries with CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID (installed libc), emits only >10ms and uses original 100/s absolute offers for a bounded60s graph0 diagnostic. This cannot reproduce every intermittent 15-minute failure or establish their sole cause. Two clock queries per phase add measurement cost; removed before final qualification.

Baseline diagnostic completed61.17s, exact6000 normalized/admitted/completed/reference/handoff prices and joined cleanup. One slow phase: idle17,402,542ns wall,20,167ns CPU. This demonstrates waiting beyond nominal1.5ms, not a CPU bottleneck or attribution of C17's100ms maxima. A release self-check accidentally overlapped the last part of this diagnostic; therefore its aggregate resource/timing values are not clean calibration and no performance conclusion is drawn. The earlier slow-idle observation preceded overlap. Compiler/profiler was absent.

Correction: mpsc poll_recv registers a Waker on the same existing sole receiver. Its notification sets a mutex-protected sticky flag and signals a Condvar; idle-only wait remains bounded by1.5ms but returns on arrivals. Notifications before wait are retained; notification during wait releases it. Stop/membership/advance/publication remain between every frame, all eight slots share32MiB, and no post-frame wait was added. This addresses the demonstrated arrival-blind wait; residual processing/descheduling delays remain possible and must pass unchanged qualification.

The focused arrival regression covers before-wait and during-wait arrival with a deliberately long2s idle timeout, requiring notification completion within500ms. The initial thread park/unpark version failed because intervening blocking synchronization can consume the thread park token; discarded in favor of the condition-variable flag. With notification-aware receive it passes in0.02s. Restoring try_recv (same former behavior) makes it fail in2.01s at the exact wake assertion. Final implementation restored. Test-fixture compile corrections (missing Instant argument and accidental command_rx replacement) were corrected before this evidence; those errors were not production diagnoses. The existing serialized queue-accounting test uses the same poll_intake path; no early removal/relabeling of pending receipts.

Campaign plan now drives the actual case loop, with a pre-resource qualification assertion requiring the exact15 ordered tuples, three graphs × five original profiles/rates/durations. The ordinary self-check accepts the complete plan and rejects the preflight plan, one-graph subset, each deleted case and each altered graph/label/rate/duration. Existing identity, sample/count omission, resource-query cadence, joined cleanup and fail-fast tests remain. Qualification report completeness/telemetry/fixture identities still use the original native checks and external checker, not process exit.

### C19 diagnostic outputs and limits

Corrected diagnostic with broad phase probes completed6000/6000 current handoffs; max admission15.677834ms. It also captured advance-control75.431ms wall/0.236708ms CPU; no attribution to CPU computation. A second bounded60s trace split snapshot, coverage, primary/reference boundaries. It completed6000/6000, admissionp993.16ms/max15.490834ms/oldest15.607292ms. Remaining slow phases included idle26.704292ms/0.020416ms CPU, decode/evaluate14.687417ms/0.815875ms CPU and primary10.979542ms/0.210500ms CPU. It did not reproduce the75ms advance stall. These are intermittent wall stalls at multiple boundaries, not proof of allocator/host/other-application fault. No further unchanged diagnostic repetition is selected. The notification fix has direct race regression evidence; the bounded traces cannot guarantee long-run maxima. Final unchanged numerical gates remain authoritative.

Temporary probes call thread CPU clocks around each phase and have additional overhead; no qualification uses them. Initial park/unpark prototype failed the before-wait regression because intervening synchronization can consume a thread's park token. It was replaced by the sticky Condvar signal; the corrected regression passed both races. Restoring old non-notifying try_recv behavior made that same check fail (exit101); no production behavior is inferred from the fixture-compilation errors corrected beforehand.

Exact controller used for the real attempt (temporary local file, durable protocol preserved here):

```python
import os, pathlib, signal, subprocess, sys, time, json, re
binary = str(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve())
test = sys.argv[2]
limit = float(sys.argv[3])
root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[4]); root.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
env = os.environ.copy(); env['METTEN_DIAGNOSTIC_CAPTURE_DIR'] = str(root)
owned = None
samples = []
def interrupted(signum, frame):
    raise RuntimeError('capture controller interrupted')
for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT): signal.signal(sig, interrupted)
try:
    with (root/'native.log').open('w') as output:
        owned = subprocess.Popen([binary, '--exact', test, '--ignored', '--nocapture'], stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=env)
        deadline = time.monotonic()+limit
        seen = set()
        while owned.poll() is None:
            if time.monotonic() > deadline: raise TimeoutError('owned diagnostic lifetime exceeded')
            for marker in root.glob('ready-*'):
                if not re.fullmatch(r'ready-\d+-\d+', marker.name) or marker.name in seen: continue
                seen.add(marker.name)
                assert marker.name.startswith(f'ready-{owned.pid}-'), 'unexpected marker owner'
                command = subprocess.check_output(['/bin/ps','-p',str(owned.pid),'-o','comm='], text=True).strip()
                assert command == binary, (command, binary)
                destination = root/(marker.name+'.sample')
                try:
                    if os.environ.get('METTEN_TEST_SAMPLE_FAILURE') == '1': raise RuntimeError('injected sampler failure')
                    r = subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/sample',str(owned.pid),'0.1','1','-file',str(destination)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, timeout=5)
                    samples.append({'pid':owned.pid,'command':command,'marker':marker.name,'exit':r.returncode,'output':r.stdout,'file':str(destination)})
                except Exception as exc:
                    samples.append({'pid':owned.pid,'marker':marker.name,'error':str(exc)})
                finally:
                    os.kill(owned.pid, signal.SIGCONT)
            time.sleep(0.001)
        print(json.dumps({'pid':owned.pid,'exit':owned.returncode,'samples':samples}))
        sys.exit(owned.returncode)
finally:
    if owned is not None and owned.poll() is None:
        os.kill(owned.pid, signal.SIGCONT)
        try: owned.wait(timeout=6)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            owned.terminate()
            try: owned.wait(timeout=3)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                owned.kill(); owned.wait()
```

Administrator access is a prerequisite for the chosen next trace method, not a proved fix or a guarantee that SIP permits the necessary probes. Freeze diagnostic design at C27 until the tracing capability gate has a concrete outcome.

If unavailable, stop before a workload run and present the exact missing capability plus one supported alternative and its concrete access/cost/scope implication. 2. **One causal experiment, original graph1 history100/s, <=900s offers.** Only after capability proof; no process pausing or worker CPU queries, same absolute offers/byte mix/large frames/meaningful observations/native contention. If timeout or evidence missing, report that precise outcome and which hypothesis remains open; no unchanged retry/calibration. On pass freeze exact source/test executable/package/environment/workload and unchanged numerical limits BEFORE separate all15-case qualification. Require complete counts/identities/dispositions/samples/delays, OS resources and joined cleanup. Any post-freeze change invalidates affected evidence. Only all required final gates passed completes step6.

## Adversarial critique of completion strategy

Owner requested one adversarial sub-agent critique. Independent native Sol reviewer adversarial_step6_plan received a fresh read-only brief without parent history, did its own published-instruction discovery at main/b8af03b3a5c8ebf945f5d798a4e05a955cc07593, and reviewed bounded original source/contract/evidence. No code changes, workloads, privileged probes or additional delegates. No scores requested/invented. Lead freshly verified the same remote/default/guidance baseline and source conditions at delivery; no guidance changes.

**Verdict: executable with changes; not cleared for a causal run unchanged.** Two material findings, both confirmed by the lead:

1. **First threshold crossing is not necessarily a useful causal incident.** Gate2 says preserve a useful natural event, but tests.rs DelayTrace::pressure3525 sets a sticky trigger at20ms; observer accounting unavailable for20ms can also set it. campaign6292 stops500ms after that first trigger, without checking usefulness or relation to the original refusal. C26 demonstrates the consequence: stopped92.93s after23ms admission delay,9298 complete handoffs/no refusal. Historical publication max100ms/p99<=20ms do not make one23ms sample evidence of the76ms/eight-slot refusal mechanism. **Confirmed plan/implementation mismatch.** Required correction before launch: predeclare the observable original-failure-relevant signature and discriminating trace evidence, then reconcile the controller's terminal stop with it. A20ms event can retain context without automatically terminating the whole900s opportunity; missing accounting evidence must remain distinct from actual delayed work. If retaining the existing rule, explicitly scope it as attribution of the first20ms event and do not claim it provides900s of C19 reproduction opportunity or licenses a correction of C19 without a demonstrated connection. No numerical performance gate is changed by diagnostic event selection.
2. **Trace visibility alone does not establish trustworthy causal evidence.** Gate1 checks thread identity, states and clock correlation, but omits explicit trace loss/incident coverage and collector-cost checks. C26 showed measurement can contaminate attribution; removing worker CPU queries does not prove a new kernel collector harmless. **Confirmed missing validation requirement.** Add to the existing controlled capability exercise: target-only ownership, collector cost, record-loss status, complete coverage across the known wait/runnable intervals and stated clock-correlation uncertainty. Missing history or material collector disturbance means inconclusive, not a production bottleneck. A short control cannot prove zero disturbance; preserve that limit. No new framework or extra long campaign is needed.

Reviewer supports existing boundaries: administrator access is neither proved usable nor the only possible approach; the capability check is a reasonable bounded next action conditional on access. One attempt can yield causal evidence or an honest inconclusive stop, not guaranteed convergence. A proved host/envelope conflict requires owner scope decision; calibration/freeze/separate15-case qualification, unchanged limits, focused regression, existing ownership and joined cleanup remain sound.

Lead disposition: accept both findings. The capability check may proceed when authorized/access is available, but the long causal run remains gated on collector-quality validation and an executable incident-selection rule. These are bounded corrections to the existing plan/harness, not a new design or broader audit. They are NOT implemented or validated by this critique-only task. No claim of full plan acceptance, step6 completion or qualified performance.

### Corrected conclusions from original material

1. **C29 clock information can be recovered for the retained first worker.** Read Apple's published scheduler source at the exact OS base tag xnu-12377.81.4 (this host reports xnu-12377.81.4~5; published source is not a claim of identical private build/configuration). MACH_BLOCK is emitted by the blocking worker before thread selection/invocation; a subsequent MACH_DISPATCH emitted on that worker executes before its return to user code. Original controlled phase begins before sleep, and event86 occurs after sleep returns. Thus a trace-origin offset O must satisfy `kernel_resume-native_resume <= O <= kernel_block-native_begin`. No visual timestamp alignment or assumption that JSON is absolute is needed. The unique>40ms worker block is61,877,667ns; native controlled wait61,885,292ns. Raw origin interval9,968,206,875–9,968,214,500ns (width7,625ns); with conservative1us expansion each side,9,968,205,875–9,968,215,500ns (width9,625ns).1210 separate idle intervals containing kernel blocks are consistent with that fixed bound. This is an independent holdout consistency check, not proof of no missing kernel events or long-run drift. The previous blanket statement that C29 clock correlation could not be established is superseded for this retained first-worker interval only. Other two workers have no external coverage.

2. **Actual native replay proves the collector hid loss.** Using published kdebug_private.h's64-bit kd_buf/RAW_header/kd_threadmap ABI, generated a tiny legacy raw trace with one synthetic worker (TID7, PID123), MACH_BLOCK at24,000,000 ticks and MACH_DISPATCH at25,440,000 ticks; a second fixture inserts TRACE_LOST_EVENTS(debugid0x07020008, PID-1/TID0) between them. Installed `/usr/bin/ktrace trace -R` reads these files without privilege or live collection. NDJSON gives0/60,000,000ns despite `-t`: JSON times are relative in this actual format. Text `-t` gives the original exact24,000,000/25,440,000 ticks. This independently verifies the future clock format.

   More importantly, replaying the injected-loss fixture with either `-p 123` OR `-f S0x0140` hides TRACE_LOST_EVENTS while still exiting0 and emitting no stderr warning. Adding S0x0702 preserves loss only when the PID filter is removed. Thus loss status was genuinely unverifiable with C29's exact command even if its one discarded line had been blank. Offline replay emits one trailing blank line; that explains a plausible origin for C29's malformed-line count, but its actual discarded bytes are unavailable and are not retroactively declared harmless.

   Prepared corrected command uses text absolute ticks, `-f S0x0140,S0x0702`, no collector PID filter; owned-worker filtering occurs after integrity handling. Kernel source at the same Apple tag explicitly emits TRACE_LOST_EVENTS on wrapped/stolen event storage when wrapping is enabled; the live gate must confirm that mode. Parser preserves unknown nonempty lines as errors, explicitly recognizes header/blank lines, handles loss/retrograde globally before owned filtering, and never treats filtered output/exit0 as no-loss proof. Self-checks exercise the real CLI's loss record, absolute timestamps, function-duration layout and an unknown-line rejection. Old filtered variants are negative controls. No second live trace was used to develop these corrections.

3. **The original arrival check covered5ms, not the observed service-gap scale.** Actual offer_schedule now has an ordinary focused check at65/76/100ms. Without a replay, the original100/s schedule has9/10/10 raw arrivals in those windows; with replay,10/11/11. All exceed8 slots. This shows how a service pause of the observed magnitude can produce explicit raw refusal with unchanged offers and caps. It does not prove a host pause caused C19, supply its missing scheduler history, or license more slots/smoothing/dropped observations. The original performance contract already disclaims arbitrary OS-pause guarantees; these counts sharpen the bound without changing acceptance. No production correction follows from arrival arithmetic alone.

4. **A separate synchronous-wake hazard is demonstrated.** Inspected actual pinned Tokio chan.rs: send pushes the item and invokes rx_waker.wake inline. Current IntakeWake::wake_by_ref takes notified's mutex. A temporary controlled native regression registers that receiver, holds its notification mutex to model a descheduled critical section, and calls actual public admit on another thread. Admission does not return within100ms; releasing the mutex allows it to finish. Test fails at the exact nonblocking-wait assertion, exit101; source restored byte-for-byte in finally. This demonstrates potential admission blocking and is a concrete candidate for correction, not proof it caused the original76ms incident. It is distinct from queue-full waiting and does not require changing slots or budgets. Pinned Rust1.100.0 Darwin parker source uses an atomic token/libdispatch semaphore signal for unpark; a possible atomic sticky flag plus captured worker Thread could avoid the application wake mutex while retaining pre-wait notifications. No production rewrite was applied: preserve current behavior for the authorized causal attempt and require a focused failing-before/passing-after race check if that correction is made. Existing C19 arrival/park-token-consumption regression must remain covered.

### C30 further falsification and justified independent correction

**Third collector defect verified offline:** the revised quality check correctly rejected retained C29 data because no MACH_MKRUNNABLE for the long-sleeping worker was retained. A second synthetic raw fixture adds a different-PID waker (TID8/PID456) making target TID7/PID123 runnable. The installed CLI emits MACH_BLOCK/MACH_MKRUNNABLE/MACH_DISPATCH without -p, but -p123 removes the relevant wake record and still exits0. A PID filter therefore hides not just loss markers but the very cross-process/kernel transition needed to separate blocked waiting from runnable delay. Corrected collection removes that output filter and retains events referring to the owned TID in scheduler arguments, plus global trace-integrity records. This is a CLI-level independently reproducible failure, not an assumed operating-system cause.

Quality-checker preparation was tested against retained C29 records converted to modeled raw ticks plus explicitly mocked mode/resource attestations. It correctly rejects missing wake coverage. Adding an explicitly modeled wake permits the positive logic branch; injected loss, eviction or excessive cost are rejected. These are parser/checker self-tests, not a live capability pass. Predeclared revised live quality checks include direct raw-Mach/local bracket correlation <=1ms, known blocked-to-runnable/CPU progress coverage, wrap/loss reporting mode, zero parse/loss/required-history failures, and combined measured collector+parser CPU <=0.1 of one core during the20s check. The cost cutoff is a diagnostic preparation choice, not a changed performance acceptance threshold. A short pass would still not prove zero disturbance.

Prior scope's deleted credential file was not reused. This is now an access blocker to collection, not a claim that unprivileged independent work is blocked.

The lead continued independent authorized engineering and removed the demonstrated application-mutex wait from IntakeWake. This is a justified correction of the reproduced wake hazard, **not attributed to the original C19 stall**. Broad step6 authority covers routine reliability corrections with focused proof; no cap/schedule/strategy/history/financial behavior was changed. The temporary original repro forces exactly the mutex dependency and demonstrates actual admit blocking. After the mutex is removed that private-field forcing mechanism no longer exists; absence of a same-form forcing seam is explicit. The replacement's source path contains an atomic store and the captured Thread's unpark, whose pinned Darwin implementation performs an atomic transition/libdispatch semaphore signal rather than waiting for the idle owner's application mutex. No claim that OS calls have a universal wall-time bound.

Production change remains in existing mod.rs:IntakeWake. It captures the existing worker Thread once at construction (SourceWorker constructs it inside that owned worker), stores a sticky AtomicBool on wake, and checks/clears it immediately before park_timeout. There is no intervening application synchronization after that check. This preserves notifications when unrelated blocking synchronization consumes the thread park token—the precise flaw in C19's earlier bare-park attempt. ```python
from pathlib import Path
import copy, hashlib, json, re, sys
COUNT_KEYS = frozenset(['active_history_complete', 'attempted_unique', 'boundary_completions', 'boundary_handoffs', 'boundary_invalidated', 'canceled_before_normalization_unique', 'canceled_before_worker_frames', 'completed', 'completed_not_published_unique', 'consumer_expected', 'consumer_frames', 'decode_capacity_frames', 'decode_rejected_frames', 'decode_stopped_frames', 'digest', 'engine_admission_refused_unique', 'engine_admitted_not_completed_unique', 'engine_admitted_unique', 'errors', 'expected_frames', 'expected_unique', 'genuine_transactions', 'handoff', 'identities_checked', 'incomplete_after_admission', 'invalidated', 'non_price_completed_transactions', 'non_price_normalized_transactions', 'normalized', 'not_attempted', 'not_attempted_frames', 'offered_frames', 'raw_admitted_frames', 'raw_admitted_unique', 'raw_refused_frames', 'reference_verified_unique', 'rejected_unique', 'resynchronization_transactions', 'socket_failed_frames', 'socket_received_frames', 'suppressed_duplicate_frames', 'unexplained_completed_loss'])
BYTE_KEYS = frozenset(['canceled_before_worker_wire', 'consumer_wire', 'decode_rejected_wire', 'decoded_wire', 'expected_wire', 'ingress_peak', 'not_attempted_wire', 'offered_wire', 'raw_admitted_wire', 'raw_refused_wire', 'socket_failed_wire', 'socket_received_wire'])
RESOURCE_KEYS = frozenset(['resource_query_calls', 'resource_query_total_ns', 'resource_query_max_ns', 'suppressed_identical_empty_clocks', 'adapter_peak', 'allocation_calls_including_harness', 'allocation_observation_wall_s', 'bounded_diagnostic_bytes', 'deallocation_calls_including_harness', 'engine_accounted_peak', 'native_view_reads', 'oldest_pending_age_max_ns', 'probe_inline_bytes', 'processing_canceled_receipt', 'queued_canceled_frames', 'raw_highwater', 'reference_engine_accounted_peak', 'rss_cpu_end', 'rss_cpu_start', 'rust_live_bytes_including_harness', 'sampled_live_peak_including_harness', 'sampled_rss_peak', 'setup_allocation_calls', 'setup_ns', 'shutdown_ns', 'steady_sampled_live_range', 'strategy_preview_saves'])
HISTOGRAMS = ['admission', 'boundary_completion', 'boundary_publication', 'completion', 'offered_frame_to_loopback_receipt', 'publication', 'sampled_clock_to_complete', 'source', 'startup_clock_to_complete', 'synthetic_coverage_to_complete']
ROOT = Path('/Users/connormoulton/.t3/worktrees/metten/t3-5ff0c48e-8b502ba4b606ca11')
EXECUTABLE = ROOT / "target/release/build/metten/64aabbdc086925d0/out/metten-64aabbdc086925d0"
SOURCE_FILES = ["crates/engine/src/sources.rs", "crates/engine/tests/sources.rs"] + ["src-tauri/src/providers/"+n+".rs" for n in ["mod","memory","source","tests","kalshi","transport"]]
OFFER_KEYS = ["attempted", "admitted", "transactions", "admitted_transactions", "bytes", "admitted_bytes", "late", "max_lateness_ns", "max_timer_overrun_ns", "max_carryover_lateness_ns", "max_intake_lock_wait_ns"]
def provider_fields(line):
    values = {}
    for k in OFFER_KEYS:
        match = re.search(r"\b"+k+r": (\d+)", line)
        if match is None: return None
        values[k] = int(match.group(1))
    if any(values[k] > values["max_lateness_ns"] for k in ["max_timer_overrun_ns", "max_carryover_lateness_ns"]): return None
    return values

def shape(r):
    try:
        if set(r["counts"]) != COUNT_KEYS or set(r["bytes"]) != BYTE_KEYS or set(r["resources"]) != RESOURCE_KEYS: return False
        if not all(type(v) is int and v >= 0 for section in ["counts","bytes"] for v in r[section].values()): return False
        q = r["resources"]
        if not all(type(q[k]) is int and q[k] >= 0 for k in ["resource_query_calls", "resource_query_total_ns", "resource_query_max_ns"]): return False
        if not 2 <= q["resource_query_calls"] <= q["native_view_reads"] + 3: return False
        if q["resource_query_total_ns"] < q["resource_query_max_ns"]: return False
        c = r["counts"]
        if c["non_price_completed_transactions"] > c["non_price_normalized_transactions"]: return False
        for name in HISTOGRAMS:
            h = r["latency"][name]
            if set(h) != {"count","max_ns","over_20ms","p50_upper_ns","p95_upper_ns","p99_upper_ns"}: return False
            if not all(type(h[k]) is int and h[k] >= 0 for k in ["count","max_ns","over_20ms"]): return False
            if not all((h[k] is None if h["count"] == 0 else type(h[k]) is int and h[k] >= 0) for k in ["p50_upper_ns","p95_upper_ns","p99_upper_ns"]): return False
        for key in ["rss_cpu_start","rss_cpu_end"]:
            v = r["resources"][key]
            if not isinstance(v,list) or len(v)!=3 or not all(type(n) is int and n>=0 for n in v): return False
        return True
    except (KeyError,TypeError,ValueError): return False

def identity():
    assert hashlib.sha256((ROOT/"target/release/metten").read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="b951d400b75b01c015d4d70b35599d8f3d763a710edb6920a09c09aeb5be191a", "application changed"
    assert hashlib.sha256(EXECUTABLE.read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="d0f0e65f76335dae4c66965624da3aa1376b217c0b750c6ad4553ccb7acccdd2", "executable changed"
    manifest = "".join(hashlib.sha256((ROOT/p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()+"  "+p+"\n" for p in SOURCE_FILES)
    assert hashlib.sha256(manifest.encode()).hexdigest()=="df343a029946d183bd50624ee79d8d5bc94f9871c4ff0a98cc92ade017cbfdb6", "source changed"
    assert hashlib.sha256((ROOT/"docs/sources/performance.md").read_bytes()).hexdigest()=="70b6ca796c74dcb22dc39ddb047328829e6f950523bb81e861212461136cea86", "contract changed"

def negative_checks(path):
    reports = [json.loads(l[12:]) for l in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if l.startswith("CALIBRATION {")]
    assert len(reports)==12
    for r in reports:
        assert shape(r)
        for section, keys in [("counts",COUNT_KEYS),("bytes",BYTE_KEYS),("resources",RESOURCE_KEYS)]:
            for key in keys:
                omitted=copy.deepcopy(r); del omitted[section][key]
                assert not shape(omitted), (section,key)
        for name in HISTOGRAMS:
            omitted=copy.deepcopy(r); del omitted["latency"][name]["count"]
            assert not shape(omitted), name
    lines = [l for l in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if l.startswith("CALIBRATION offers ")]
    assert len(lines) == 36
    for line in lines:
        assert provider_fields(line) is not None
        for key in OFFER_KEYS:
            omitted = re.sub(r"\b"+key+r": \d+,? ?", "", line, count=1)
            assert provider_fields(omitted) is None, key
    identity()
    print("PREQUALIFICATION_COMPLETENESS passed: all required field/sample omissions rejected")

def check(path):
    identity()
    text=Path(path).read_text(); reports=[]; offers=[]; verdicts=[]
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("CALIBRATION {"):
            reports.append(json.loads(line[12:])); offers.append([])
        elif line.startswith("CALIBRATION offers "):
            assert offers, "orphan provider disposition"
            provider=int(re.search(r"provider=(\d+)",line).group(1))
            values=provider_fields(line)
            assert values is not None, "missing/invalid provider phase telemetry"
            offers[-1].append((provider,values))
        elif line.startswith("QUALIFICATION "):
            verdicts.append(json.loads(line[14:]))
    profiles=[("warmup",100,30),("low",100,900),("medium",1000,900),("burst",10000,1),("quiet",0,60)]
    expected=[(g,label,rate,seconds) for g in range(3) for label,rate,seconds in profiles]
    assert len(reports)==len(verdicts)==len(offers)==15, "missing case/report/verdict"
    for r,v,oo,(g,label,rate,seconds) in zip(reports,verdicts,offers,expected):
        assert (r["graph"],r["case"],r["rate"],r["duration_s"])==(g,label,rate,seconds)
        assert r["qualification"] is True and shape(r), (g,label,"missing required telemetry")
        assert (v["graph"],v["case"],v["contract"],v["passed"])==(g,label,"issue-5-step-6-v1",True), (g,label,"native qualification gate failed")
        assert [p for p,_ in oo]==[0,1,2], (g,label,"missing provider dispositions")
        c,b=r["counts"],r["bytes"]
        for offered,section,key in [("attempted",c,"offered_frames"),("admitted",c,"raw_admitted_frames"),("transactions",c,"attempted_unique"),("admitted_transactions",c,"raw_admitted_unique"),("bytes",b,"offered_wire"),("admitted_bytes",b,"raw_admitted_wire")]:
            assert sum(o[offered] for _,o in oo)==section[key], (g,label,offered)
        assert all(o["late"]<=o["attempted"] for _,o in oo)
        if rate<=100:
            assert all(o["max_lateness_ns"]<=100_000_000 for _,o in oo), (g,label,"supported offer lateness exceeded")
    def os_value(label):
        m=re.search(r"^\s*(\d+)\s+"+re.escape(label)+r"$",text,re.M)
        assert m, "missing OS "+label
        return int(m.group(1))
    rss=os_value("maximum resident set size"); footprint=os_value("peak memory footprint"); swaps=os_value("swaps")
    assert rss<=256*1024*1024 and footprint<=256*1024*1024 and swaps==0, "OS resource contract failed"
    assert "test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed;" in text, "native process did not pass"
    m=re.search(r"^\s*(\d+\.\d+) real\s+", text, re.M)
    assert m, "missing OS wall duration"
    observed=sum(r["resources"]["setup_ns"]/1e9+r["resources"]["allocation_observation_wall_s"] for r in reports)
    residual=float(m.group(1))-observed
    assert residual>=-0.02, "per-case observation windows overlap OS duration"
    cleanup_bound=max(r["resources"]["shutdown_ns"] for r in reports)/1e9+max(0,residual)+0.02
    assert cleanup_bound<=5, "combined source/socket/storage cleanup bound exceeded"
    print(json.dumps({"all_unobserved_process_gaps_s":residual,"conservative_combined_cleanup_bound_s":cleanup_bound},sort_keys=True))
    print(json.dumps({"contract":"issue-5-step-6-v1","qualified":True,"cases":15,"provider_dispositions":45,"os_max_rss_bytes":rss,"os_peak_footprint_bytes":footprint,"swaps":swaps,"log_sha256":hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()},sort_keys=True))

if __name__=="__main__":
    if sys.argv[1]=="--self-check": negative_checks(sys.argv[2])
    else: check(sys.argv[1])

## Fixed correctness and accounting gates

Supported cases require every expected price normalized, admitted, primarily completed,
